name: Viktor Tsybulenko
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Soviet national javelin title in 1952 and competed at the Helsinki Olympics, finishing fourth, while being ranked in the world top 10.
early_history_summary: Tsybulenko emerged from the Soviet athletics system in the early 1950s, winning his first Soviet national javelin title in 1952 at age 22 and immediately competing at the Helsinki Olympics. He remained in the world top 10 from 1952 onward, establishing himself as the top Soviet javelin thrower of the decade.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical talent and Soviet sports pipeline
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Born in Vepryk, Kyiv Oblast, Ukrainian SSR.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet sports system, athletics pipeline, physical talent
evidence_summary: Tsybulenko won the Soviet national javelin title in 1952 at age 22 and competed at the Helsinki Olympics, establishing himself as a world-class thrower well before 26. The Soviet sports system provided an elite institutional pipeline, though specific family background and early training details are not documented in reviewed sources. His world top-10 ranking from 1952 and multiple Soviet titles confirm sustained elite-level performance from his early twenties.

name: Gottfried Helnwein
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Master-class prize (Meisterschulpreis) of the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, the Kardinal-König prize, and the Theodor-Körner prize during his studies, completing his degree by 1973.
early_history_summary: Helnwein grew up in postwar Vienna in a strict Catholic household and enrolled at the Higher Federal Institution for Graphic Education in 1965 at age 17. He began provocative self-performance art as a teenager and progressed to the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna (1969-1973), where he won multiple prestigious student prizes and developed his hyperrealistic style depicting wounded children.
family_context_summary: Born in Vienna shortly after World War II; father Joseph worked for the Austrian Post and Telegraphy administration, mother Margarethe was a housewife. Strict Roman Catholic upbringing in a bleak postwar city.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Father was a postal worker, mother a housewife; no family connection to the arts documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: postwar Vienna, Catholic upbringing, Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, early performance art
evidence_summary: Helnwein enrolled at a graphic arts institution at 17 and progressed to the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, winning the Master-class prize, Kardinal-König prize, and Theodor-Körner prize by age 25 in 1973. His upbringing in devastated postwar Vienna and strict Catholic environment shaped his provocative artistic vision. No family financial or domain advantages are documented; his early trajectory appears driven by personal compulsion and institutional training rather than inherited resources.
starting_point: Born in 1948 in Vienna, Austria, shortly after World War II; son of a postal worker and a housewife, raised in a strict Catholic household in a devastated postwar city.
current_position: Austrian-Irish visual artist, age 77, living and working between Ireland (Castle Gurteen de la Poer) and Los Angeles; internationally exhibited with major retrospectives including at the Albertina Museum in Vienna.

trajectory.event: Enrolled at the Higher Federal Institution for Graphic Education and Experimentation in Vienna.

Received Irish citizenship.

name: Johan Andersson
milestone_by_age_26: Was a key programmer on the original Europa Universalis (2000), having joined the development team in 1998, and previously worked as a programmer at Funcom on Sega Genesis games from 1994.
early_history_summary: Andersson began his career as a programmer at Funcom in 1994 at age 19-20, working on Sega Genesis titles. In 1998 he joined the team that would become Paradox Interactive, contributing to the original Europa Universalis board-game adaptation released in 2000. He grew up playing Civilization and board games, which directly shaped his grand strategy game design philosophy.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Born in Sweden; attended Stockholm University studying Russian and Mathematics but did not complete a degree.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Swedish game development ecosystem, strategy game passion, early programming career, Funcom
evidence_summary: Andersson started programming professionally at Funcom in 1994 at age 19-20 and joined the Europa Universalis team in 1998, with the game releasing in 2000 when he was 26. His deep personal passion for strategy games and board games, cultivated from childhood, directly translated into his career path. Sweden's growing game development ecosystem provided a frontier geography advantage, though no family financial or domain advantages are documented.
starting_point: Born in 1974 in Sweden; family background not documented in reviewed sources. Attended Stockholm University briefly studying Russian and Mathematics.
current_position: Studio lead of Paradox Tinto (a division of Paradox Interactive) in Sitges, Spain, age 51; widely considered the central creative force behind Paradox's grand strategy game franchise including Europa Universalis, Hearts of Iron, and Crusader Kings.

name: Hélène Cixous
milestone_by_age_26: Passed the agrégation d'anglais in 1959, qualifying for university teaching, and began teaching at the University of Bordeaux by 1962.
early_history_summary: Cixous was born to Jewish parents in Oran, French Algeria; her father, a physician, died of tuberculosis in 1948 when she was 11. She earned the highly competitive agrégation d'anglais in 1959 at age 22, qualifying her for university-level teaching. By 1962 she was an assistante at the University of Bordeaux, and by 26 she was established in the French academic system.
family_context_summary: Born to Jewish parents in Oran, French Algeria; father Georges was a physician who died of tuberculosis in 1948, mother Eve became a midwife. Brother Pierre was condemned to death by the OAS in 1961 for supporting Algerian independence.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a physician who wrote his dissertation on tuberculosis; mother became a midwife after father's death. Educated professional family in colonial Algeria.
primary_early_advantage_tags: French academic system, agrégation, educated family, Jewish Algerian background, adversity
evidence_summary: Cixous passed the agrégation d'anglais at 22 in 1959 and was teaching at the University of Bordeaux by 25, establishing herself in the French academic system well before 26. Her father was a physician and her mother a midwife, providing an educated professional family environment despite the trauma of his early death. Growing up Jewish in French Algeria and losing her father at 11 shaped her intellectual urgency and outsider perspective. The French university pipeline provided the institutional structure for her early academic career.
starting_point: Born in 1937 in Oran, French Algeria, to Jewish parents; father was a physician, mother became a midwife after his death in 1948.
current_position: Professor emeritus at University of Paris VIII, age 88; prolific author of 70+ books and considered a strong contender for the Nobel Prize in Literature.

trajectory.event: Passed the agrégation d'anglais, qualifying for university teaching in France.

milestone_by_age_26: Made his La Liga debut in September 2000 at age 26, becoming one of the youngest referees to officiate in Spain's top football division.

A refereeing technical director recognized his ability and guided his progression through the ranks. After 13 years of climbing the Spanish refereeing pyramid, he debuted in La Liga in 2000 at age 26, later becoming a FIFA-listed referee in 2004.
family_context_summary: From Pamplona, Navarra, Spain. Father of two. Also a trained sociologist with degrees in Sociology and Political Science.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Spanish refereeing system, early start at 13, mentorship, La Liga pipeline
evidence_summary: Undiano started refereeing at 13 and spent 13 years climbing the Spanish refereeing system before his La Liga debut at 26 in 2000. A refereeing technical director identified his talent and encouraged him to work hard, providing early mentorship. He combined refereeing with university studies in sociology. No family financial or domain advantages are documented; his trajectory was driven by early specialization and the Spanish football institutional pipeline.
starting_point: Born in 1973 in Pamplona, Navarra, Spain; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired football referee, age 52; retired in 2019 after officiating the UEFA Nations League final; also a trained sociologist.

After graduating with a BA in Drama in 1977, he made his screen debut in the TV film Wilma, attended the American Conservatory Theater in San Francisco for one year, then returned to New York to pursue professional acting, landing his first Hollywood film role in Carbon Copy (1981) at age 26.
family_context_summary: Born in Mount Vernon, New York; father was a Pentecostal minister, mother owned a beauty shop. Middle-class family; parents divorced when he was 14, after which he was sent to Oakland Military Academy.

name: Gustavo Kuerten
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1997 French Open at age 20, defeating three former champions, and by age 26 had won three Grand Slam titles, reached world No. 1, and won the Masters Cup.
early_history_summary: Kuerten began playing tennis at age 6 in Florianópolis, Brazil, taught by his father Aldo, a former amateur tennis player. After his father's death when he was 8, coach Larri Passos began training him at age 14 and became his mentor for 15 years. Kuerten turned professional in 1995 at 19, won his first doubles title in 1996, and stunned the tennis world by winning the 1997 French Open as a 20-year-old ranked 66th.
family_context_summary: Born in Florianópolis, Brazil, to a middle-class family of German heritage; father Aldo was a former amateur tennis player who died of a heart attack when Kuerten was 8; mother raised the family; younger brother Guilherme had cerebral palsy.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a former amateur tennis player who taught Kuerten the game from age 6 and introduced him to coach Larri Passos. The family's tennis connection was direct and formative.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Larri Passos coaching, father tennis background, early start, family tragedy, clay-court talent
evidence_summary: Kuerten won the 1997 French Open at 20, having started tennis at 6 with his father and been coached by Larri Passos from age 14 for 15 years. His father, a former amateur tennis player, provided direct domain introduction but died when Kuerten was 8, creating financial hardship. Passos's sustained mentorship was the dominant early advantage, combining with Kuerten's natural clay-court talent. The family's middle-class status and lack of significant financial resources made the journey harder, but Passos's belief and training enabled his rapid rise from unknown to Grand Slam champion.
starting_point: Born in 1976 in Florianópolis, Brazil, to a middle-class family of German heritage; father was a former amateur tennis player who died when Kuerten was 8, mother raised the family.
current_position: Retired professional tennis player, age 49; three-time French Open champion and former world No. 1; runs the Guga Kuerten Institute for disabled people in Florianópolis; estimated net worth approximately $10-15 million.

name: Jan Palach
milestone_by_age_26: Committed self-immolation on January 16, 1969, in Wenceslas Square, Prague, as a political protest against the Soviet-led invasion of Czechoslovakia, dying three days later at age 20.
early_history_summary: Palach was a history and political economics student at Charles University in Prague who became politically active during the Prague Spring and its suppression by the Warsaw Pact invasion in August 1968. After participating in student protests and an unsuccessful occupational strike in late 1968, he decided on a radical act to awaken public resistance, setting himself on fire on January 16, 1969, and dying of his burns on January 19.
family_context_summary: Born in Všetaty, Czechoslovakia; father died when Palach was 13, and he was raised in part by his grandfather. His brother Jiří was 7 years older. An average student who was an avid reader of Jules Verne.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No family political or activist background documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Prague Spring, Soviet invasion, Charles University, political oppression, father's death
evidence_summary: Palach's self-immolation at 20 in January 1969 was one of the most iconic political protests of the 20th century, directly responding to the Soviet suppression of the Prague Spring. He was a Charles University student who had participated in protests and strikes in late 1968 before deciding on his radical act. His father's death when he was 13 and life under Soviet oppression shaped his sense of urgency. No family advantages or early domain training are relevant; his milestone was driven by political conviction and the extraordinary historical moment.
starting_point: Born in 1948 in Všetaty, Czechoslovakia; father died when Palach was 13, raised in part by his grandfather; average student from a small town.
current_position: Died on January 19, 1969, at age 20 in Prague from burns sustained in his self-immolation protest; became an enduring symbol of resistance against Soviet oppression.

name: Phil Ramone
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded A&R Recording studio in New York in 1958 at age 24, establishing himself as an independent recording engineer and studio owner before age 26.
early_history_summary: Ramone was a violin prodigy who began playing at age 3 in South Africa and performed for Princess Elizabeth at age 10. His family moved to Brooklyn, where he trained at the Juilliard School while still in high school. He apprenticed at JAC Recording studio, then co-founded A&R Recording with Jack Arnold in 1958 at age 24, building a reputation as a versatile engineer in pop and jazz.
primary_leverage_engine: Musical prodigy and technical engineering depth
family_context_summary: Born in South Africa; father died when he was young, mother worked in a department store. Family moved to Brooklyn, New York, where he grew up and trained at Juilliard.

evidence_summary: Ramone co-founded A&R Recording at 24 in 1958, having been a violin prodigy from age 3 who performed for royalty at 10 and trained at Juilliard while in high school. His father died young and his mother worked in a department store, providing no financial safety net. He apprenticed at JAC Recording before co-founding his own studio, combining rare musical depth with technical engineering skill. The New York music scene and Juilliard training provided institutional and geographic advantages, while his immigrant background and early father loss created adversity that may have accelerated his drive.
